key_insight: Discrete CNOT routing can limit not only the expressive capacity of a variational quantum circuit, but also whether training can actually access useful descent directions.
engineering_relevance: For quantum circuit design and optimization, routing choices should be treated as a trainability problem, not just a hardware-compatibility or expressivity problem.
method: Separate binary routing matrices from continuous one-qubit rotations.
Derive exact capacity and local tangent-space bounds for CNOT-routed circuits.
Use routing-conditioned identity insertion to add new descent directions without changing the current unitary.
evidence_signal: Exact-statevector experiments on Bell tasks and Heisenberg/TFIM benchmarks show strong short-horizon score-descent correlations and routing-dependent near-stagnation effects.
watch_item: The proposed scores and routing updates are evaluated in controlled settings, so their robustness on noisy hardware and larger-scale ansatzes still needs validation.
paper_title: When Expressivity Is Not Enough: Discrete Routing Geometry in Variational Quantum Circuits
